newsitem.title: UK: UK insurance brokers must spend more on IT - report.
newsitem.headline: UK insurance brokers must spend more on IT - report.

text.p: UK general insurance brokers will have to increase their investment in information technology to meet the competitive threat from direct telephone insurers in personal lines insurance.
"General insurance brokers will be in for a tough time, unless they harness technology to combat the threat from direct writers," management consultancy Datamonitor said in a report.
Insurance brokers will spend 177 million stg on IT this year, rising to 199 million in 2001, Datamonitor said in its report 'IT in UK Personal General Insurance'.
Brokers will expand their use of call centres, databases, the Internet and e-mail
However, by 2000 their share of personal general insurance will have fallen to 36 percent from 61 percent in 1995, it added.
The expansion of direct writers will lead to mergers, acquisitions and some brokers withdrawing from the personal lines market for motor and household insurance.
Brokers will have to respond to this trend by investing in direct distribution of policies over the telephone and the Internet, the report said.
